A notable clue — the image title referencing "Before and 6 Weeks After Initiating Ustekinumab Treatment" — suggests systemic biologic therapy for psoriasis may have been given, but the patient is uncertain and there is no documentation of treatment response. Critical contextual items (prior topical steroid use, response to therapies, scalp/nail involvement, detailed photos, DIF result) are missing and are important to distinguish these entities and to exclude steroid‑exacerbated dermatitis or other mimics.

- Clear documentation of prior/current topical steroid use or systemic psoriasis therapy (ustekinumab), and response to any treatments.

1. Precise treatment history

   - Record OTC/cosmetic/sunscreen use and any temporal relation to flares.

2. Targeted clinical information and images
   - High‑quality, close‑up clinical photographs of representative lesions (pre‑treatment if available) including scalp, hairline, nasolabial folds, ears, and neck.

3. Microbiologic/histologic clarification
   - Report of DIF (was requested — provide result).
   - Confirm adequacy of PAS stain; if any clinical suspicion remains for tinea, perform KOH of scale and fungal culture; consider repeat biopsy with PAS if initial sampling was superficial.
   - If biopsy sampling is questioned, consider a repeat punch from an active border.

4. Short diagnostic/therapeutic trials (documented)
   - Empiric trial with topical antifungal (e.g., ketoconazole cream/shampoo) for 2–4 weeks with documented response if seborrheic dermatitis is suspected.
   - If topical steroid use is present, document course of steroid withdrawal and clinical change to assess steroid‑exacerbated dermatitis.

5. Ancillary bedside assessment
   - Dermoscopy to identify vascular patterns suggestive of rosacea versus scaling/plaques of psoriasis/seborrhea.
   - Consider patch testing if allergic contact dermatitis to cosmetics is suspected.

Collecting these items will permit a confident single diagnosis (or appropriately justify ongoing differential) and allow an evidence‑based management plan.
